must_have_properties: Exactly 1 Clock Lane (differential pair) + 1..4 Data Lane pairs.
Clock Lane SHALL be driven only by host processor; peripheral SHALL NOT drive Clock Lane.
All DSI transmitters and receivers SHALL support Continuous Clock behavior on the Clock Lane.
Host SHALL implement minimum of one Data Lane; additional Lane capability is optional.
In a Command Mode system, Data Lane 0 SHALL be bidirectional; additional Data Lanes SHALL be unidirectional.
Forward direction Low Power transmissions SHALL use Data Lane 0 only.
Reverse-direction (peripheral → host) transmissions SHALL use Low Power Mode only and Data Lane 0 only.
Short Packets SHALL be 4 bytes long including ECC byte; Long Packets SHALL be 6..65541 bytes.
Packet Header SHALL be a 32-bit field (DI byte + Word Count LS + Word Count MS + ECC byte).
Header ECC SHALL be Hamming-modified (24,8) — single-bit-correct + 2-bit-detect over DI + WC.
P6 and P7 of ECC byte SHALL be 0 by transmitter; receiver SHALL ignore P6 and P7 and force them to 0 before processing.
Long Packet Footer SHALL be a 16-bit CRC, polynomial x^16+x^12+x^5+1, initial value 0xFFFF, LSB-first, covering payload bytes only.
Zero-byte payload Long Packet Footer SHALL be 0xFFFF.
Peripheral that does NOT calculate Checksum SHALL transmit 0x0000 in the Packet Footer.
All packet bytes SHALL be transmitted LSB-first; multi-byte fields SHALL be transmitted least-significant byte first unless otherwise specified.
Devices compliant with DSI v1.01 SHALL support EoTp Short Packet (DT=0x08, payload 0x0F0F, ECC 0x01).
Devices SHALL provide an implementation-specific means to enable/disable EoTp.
EoTp SHOULD NOT be sent when transmitting in LP mode.
Tearing Effect Trigger Message byte 0x5D is RESERVED by DSI for TE signaling only and SHALL NOT be used for any other purpose.
Set Maximum Return Packet Size (DT=0x37) default value at power-on or reset SHALL be 1.
Set Maximum Return Packet Size SHALL be ignored by peripherals with unidirectional DSI interfaces.
Host SHALL implement ECC and Checksum capabilities; ECC and Checksum capabilities SHALL be separately enable/disable so host can match a peripheral's capability.
Peripheral SHALL implement ECC; Checksum implementation is optional for peripheral.
Bidirectional peripheral SHALL implement HRX_TO and LTX-P_TO.
Host SHALL implement HTX_TO and LRX-H_TO.
LRX-H_TO MUST be set longer than LTX-P_TO.
Host LP clock frequency SHALL be 67%..150% of peripheral LP clock frequency.
Host T_INIT_MASTER at power-up SHALL be ≥ t_POR + T_INIT_SLAVE + T_INTERNAL_DELAY of the peripheral.
Peripheral SHALL power up in RX-Stop and SHALL ignore all Link states until T_INIT_SLAVE elapses.
After every BTA: peripheral SHALL respond with one or more appropriate packets, then return bus ownership to host with its own BTA.
Errors SHALL be accumulated by the peripheral until reported via Acknowledge and Error Report, then cleared from the Error Register.

Following any command, if SoT Error / SoT Sync Error / DSI VC ID Invalid / DSI Protocol Violation is detected or the DSI command is not recognized, peripheral SHALL send a 4-byte Acknowledge and Error Report; no read or write access SHALL take place.
Bit 7 and Bit 14 of Error Report SHALL be transmitted as 0 (Reserved).
Video Mode peripheral SHALL implement at least one of the four pixel formats: 16-bpp RGB565, 18-bpp RGB666 Packed, 18-bpp RGB666 Loosely Packed, 24-bpp RGB888. Host SHALL implement all four.
Host SHALL implement one or more of the Display Resolutions in Table 23.
Data Type codes with DT[3:0] = 0b0000 or 0b1111 SHALL NOT be used.
Multi-Lane implementations SHALL use a single common Clock Lane shared by all Data Lanes.
must_not_have_properties: Peripheral SHALL NOT drive Clock Lane under any circumstances.
Reverse direction HS transmission is NOT permitted; peripheral-to-host data SHALL use LP only.
Reserved bits (Error Report bits 7 and 14) SHALL NOT carry data.
DSI v1.0 devices SHALL NOT advertise EoTp support.
EoTp SHALL NOT be sent on LP transmissions.
Trigger Message byte 0x5D SHALL NOT be used for any purpose other than Tearing Effect.
Reserved Data Type codes SHALL NOT be used; using them triggers DSI DT Not Recognized error.
DT codes with DT[3:0] = 0b0000 or 0b1111 SHALL NOT be transmitted (DO NOT USE class).
P6 and P7 of ECC byte SHALL NOT be set to 1 by transmitter.

compliance_failure_modes.trigger: 2-bit error in header → packet dropped + Error Report bit 9 set; rest of transmission lost (boundary lost).
Long-Packet payload corruption → Error Report bit 10 set.
Receiver got unknown DT → bit 11 set; packet boundary lost.
Header VC not recognized → bit 12 set.
WC mismatch between header and payload bytes received → bit 13 set.
Expected EoTp not received or expected BTA not received after read → bit 15 set.
HRX_TO expired during HS RX → bit 5 set; peripheral returns to LP-RX.
PHY-detected Start-of-Transmission corrupted → bit 0 or bit 1 set.
LP Escape command unrecognized → bit 3 set.
LP-CD asserts LP-High or LP-Low Fault on bidirectional Data Lane 0; Annex A recovery flow runs.

fields.reset_behavior_compliance: On power-on or LP-Escape Reset: both ends drive LP-11 Stop state; peripheral powers up in RX-Stop with Maximum Return Packet Size = 1; no DSI Protocol state survives reset.
fields.min_clock_constraint: Determined by D-PHY v0.90.00 — typically ≥ 40 MHz Clock Lane (80 Mbps data rate); maximum bound also from D-PHY.
